sections.title: Basic Concept of Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.content: Subject-Verb Agreement means that the Subject and Verb in a sentence must match in number (Singular/Plural). If the Subject is singular, a singular verb is used. If the Subject is plural, a plural verb is used.

sections.title: Subjects Joined by 'And'
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether two different persons or things are connected by 'and'. Step 2: If they represent two different subjects, the verb will be plural. Step 3: If both together represent a single idea or unit, the verb will be singular. Example: 'Ram and Shyam are friends.' But 'Bread and butter is my breakfast.'

sections.title: Use of 'Each', 'Every', 'Either', 'Neither'
sections.content: Step 1: Look for 'each', 'every', 'either', or 'neither' in the subject. Step 2: These words are always treated as singular. Step 3: Therefore, the verb will also be singular. Example: 'Each student is ready.'

sections.title: Collective Nouns
sections.content: Step 1: Identify collective nouns (team, committee, jury). Step 2: If the group acts as a single unit, use a singular verb. Step 3: If the members act individually, use a plural verb. Example: 'The team is winning.' But 'The team are arguing among themselves.'

sections.title: Rule of 'Either...or' and 'Neither...nor'
sections.content: Step 1: Identify both subjects. Step 2: Check which subject is closest to the verb. Step 3: The verb agrees with the nearest subject. Example: 'Either Ram or his friends are coming.'

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Maintaining correct agreement between the subject and verb is essential. 'And' usually takes a plural verb, 'Each/Every/Either/Neither' take singular verbs, collective nouns depend on context, and in 'Either...or' structures the verb agrees with the nearest subject.

tricks.title: 'And' Shortcut Rule
tricks.explanation: If two different subjects are joined by 'and', the verb will usually be plural.

tricks.title: Single Idea Rule
tricks.explanation: If words joined by 'and' represent a single idea, the verb will be singular.
tricks.example: Bread and butter is my breakfast.

tricks.title: Each/Every Rule
tricks.explanation: Each and Every are always treated as singular subjects.

tricks.title: Either/Neither Quick Check
tricks.explanation: Match the verb with the subject nearest to it.
tricks.example: Neither the teacher nor the students are ready.

tricks.title: Collective Noun Meaning Check
tricks.explanation: If the group acts as one unit, use a singular verb.

tricks.title: Members Acting Individually
tricks.explanation: If the members act separately, use a plural verb.
tricks.example: The committee are debating the issue.

tricks.title: Quick Subject Finder
tricks.explanation: Identify the real subject before the verb and do not get confused by words in between.
tricks.example: Each of the players is ready.

tricks.title: Either/Or Practice Trick
tricks.explanation: If the subjects differ in number, follow the one closest to the verb.
tricks.example: Either the boys or the teacher is responsible.
